title: Why the Universe Only Allows One Black Hole at Rest
hook: Could two black holes sit perfectly still beside each other forever? A new proof says no — in the stationary vacuum case, the pull between them is always attractive, so Kerr stands alone.
key_points: The uniqueness conjecture says a stationary rotating vacuum black hole must be the Kerr solution.
The gap was ruling out configurations with more than one horizon held in static balance.
The authors prove no such multi-horizon configuration exists when every degenerate piece spins.
The mechanism: the interaction force along the axis between horizons is always attractive.
Technically that follows from a strictly negative angle defect along every finite axis rod.
A corollary establishes the conjectured mass-angular-momentum inequality for multiple black holes.
content_html: General relativity has a striking tidiness result at its core: a black hole sitting quietly in empty space, rotating and unchanging, has to be the Kerr solution. Mass and spin, nothing else. The "no-hair" slogan captures the idea, but the full theorem has had a stubborn hole in it — nobody had ruled out configurations containing more than one horizon, arranged so their pulls somehow balanced and the whole thing stayed still.
extra_html:
Qing Han, Marcus Khuri, Gilbert Weinstein and Jingang Xiong report a proof closing that case, in the axially symmetric, stationary vacuum setting, under the condition that every degenerate horizon component carries non-zero angular momentum. Their conclusion is physically intuitive even though the machinery is not: in any candidate multi-horizon configuration, the interaction force along the axis joining the horizons is always attractive. There is nothing to push back, so the arrangement cannot hold still, and only the single-horizon Kerr solution survives.

The technical statement is that the logarithmic angle defect along every finite axis rod — the conical singularity you would need to insert as a strut to prop the horizons apart — is strictly negative. Getting there takes a refined asymptotic analysis of the associated singular harmonic maps, drawing on a companion paper, plus a global bound on the Weyl conformal factor from a scalar-curvature differential inequality. As a corollary of the extremal version, the authors also obtain the conjectured mass-angular momentum inequality for multiple dynamical black holes.

related.title: Black Holes
related.hook: A black hole is a place where gravity wins so completely that nothing — not even light — can escape once it crosses the edge called the event horizon.

related.title: Precision Ringdown Measurements of Binary Black Hole Remnants
related.hook: After two black holes merge, the remnant 'rings' like a struck bell — general relativity says that tone depends only on its mass and spin. A sharper measurement says: still true.

related.title: General Relativity: Gravity Is Geometry
related.hook: Einstein's biggest idea: gravity isn't a force pulling objects, it's the bending of spacetime by mass and energy. Matter curves space; curved space steers matter.

related.title: Ten Years of Listening to Black Holes Spin
related.hook: A decade after the first gravitational-wave detection, 100+ events let astronomers read black holes' spins — and spin turns out to reveal how the pairs were born.

flashcards.prompt: What does black hole uniqueness claim in the stationary, axially symmetric vacuum setting?

choices.text: The Kerr solution is the only possibility — no multi-horizon configuration can sit in equilibrium
Every black hole must eventually evaporate into radiation
Black holes can only form from collapsing stars, never from other processes

flashcards.explanation_html: Uniqueness rules out exotic alternatives and balanced multi-black-hole configurations, leaving Kerr as the single stationary vacuum solution.

flashcards.prompt: What physical fact blocks two stationary black holes from coexisting?
flashcards.back_html: The interaction force along the axis between them is always attractive, so nothing holds them apart and no static equilibrium configuration can exist.
